canDo.en: I can present my achievements with concrete evidence, handle awkward questions with composure, and hedge claims about my abilities without underselling myself.
canDo.bg: Мога да представя постиженията си с конкретни доказателства, да се справя спокойно с неудобни въпроси и да смекчавам твърденията за уменията си, без да се подценявам.

title.bg: Как да се представиш, без да преувеличаваш

body.en: Strong interview answers are specific: what you did, and what changed as a result ("we cut waiting times by almost a third"). When a question is difficult, it's fine to buy a moment ("That's a good question — let me think about that"). Hedging makes claims credible rather than weak: "I'd say…", "It's fair to say…", "I wouldn't go as far as to call myself…". "Admittedly" signals that you're conceding a weakness — interviewers usually respect honesty followed by what you learnt. Avoid two extremes: bragging without evidence, and apologising for yourself.
body.bg: Силните отговори на интервю са конкретни: какво си направил/а и какво се е променило в резултат ("we cut waiting times by almost a third" — намалихме времето за чакане с почти една трета). Когато въпросът е труден, спокойно можеш да си дадеш секунда ("That's a good question — let me think about that"). Смекчаването (hedging) прави твърденията по-убедителни, а не по-слаби: "I'd say…", "It's fair to say…", "I wouldn't go as far as to call myself…". "Admittedly" показва, че признаваш слабост — интервюиращите обикновено ценят честността, последвана от това какво си научил/а. Избягвай двете крайности: хвалби без доказателства и извинения за самия себе си.

examples: I was responsible for rolling out a new booking system across three offices.
As a result, we cut waiting times by almost a third.
That's a good question — let me think about that for a moment.
I'd say my main weakness is that I tend to take on too much.
It's fair to say the project didn't go entirely to plan.
Admittedly, I underestimated how long it would take.

meaning.en: Having the job of looking after something or making sure it happens.

glossary.example: I was responsible for the budget.

meaning.en: To introduce a new system, product or service, usually in stages.
meaning.bg: Въвеждам (нова система, продукт или услуга), обикновено поетапно.

glossary.example: We rolled out the system in three months.

meaning.en: An arrangement to have a table, room, ticket or appointment.

glossary.example: I made a booking for two.

meaning.en: In every part of a group or area.

glossary.example: The change was rolled out across all offices.

meaning.en: To reduce an amount, such as a cost or a time.

glossary.example: We cut costs by a third.

meaning.en: One of three equal parts of something.

glossary.example: Almost a third of the team left.

meaning.en: A very short period of time.

glossary.example: Let me think for a moment.

meaning.en: Something you are not good at, or a part of something that is not strong.
"Tend to" + verb: to usually do something, or be likely to do it.
meaning.bg: "Tend to" + глагол: обикновено правя нещо, склонен/склонна съм да правя нещо.

meaning.en: A planned piece of work with a particular aim.
Used when you accept that something is true, often something that weakens your point.
meaning.bg: Признавам, трябва да призная — когато приемаш нещо, което отслабва позицията ти.

meaning.en: To think something is smaller, easier or less important than it really is.

objective.en: Describe an achievement with evidence, admit a mistake constructively, and explain a career gap with composure.
objective.bg: Да опишеш постижение с доказателства, да признаеш грешка градивно и спокойно да обясниш прекъсване в кариерата.

explanation.en: The best answers follow a pattern: specific action + measurable result; honest admission + what you changed; brief, unapologetic explanation + a positive bridge back to the job. Bragging, blaming others and evasive vagueness all lose trust.
explanation.bg: Най-добрите отговори следват модел: конкретно действие + измерим резултат; честно признание + какво си променил/а; кратко обяснение без извинения + положителен мост обратно към работата. Хвалбите, обвиняването на други и мъглявите отговори подкопават доверието.

hints.en: Ask yourself: does this answer give evidence, or just an opinion?
hints.bg: Запитай се: този отговор дава ли доказателство, или само мнение?

scene.en: A panel interview for a project manager role. Margaret and David are interviewing you.
scene.bg: Интервю пред комисия за позиция мениджър проекти. Интервюират те Маргарет и Дейвид.

lines.text: Thanks for coming in, Mila. Perhaps you could start by telling us about an achievement you're particularly proud of.

options.text: Certainly. In my last role I led the move to a new booking system. It took eight months, but we ended up cutting waiting times by almost a third.
Well, I'm basically the best project manager I've ever worked with, so it's hard to pick just one.

why.en: A sweeping claim with no evidence comes across as arrogant — and it dodges the question.
why.bg: Голямо твърдение без никакво доказателство звучи арогантно — и заобикаля въпроса.

options.text: Certainly. In my last role I was leading the move to a new booking system during eight months.

why.en: For a finished achievement, use the past simple ("I led"), and duration takes "for", not "during".
why.bg: За завършено постижение използвай минало просто време ("I led"), а продължителността се изразява с "for", не с "during".

lines.text: Impressive. And what would you say didn't go so well on that project?

options.text: Admittedly, I underestimated how much training staff would need, so the first few weeks were rougher than they should have been. I now build training into every plan from day one.
Honestly? Nothing. It went perfectly from start to finish.

why.en: Nobody believes a project went perfectly. It sounds either naive or evasive.
why.bg: Никой не вярва, че проект е минал перфектно. Звучи или наивно, или уклончиво.

options.text: Admittedly, most of the problems were caused by my colleagues in IT.

why.en: Blaming others is a red flag in interviews. Own your part and say what you learnt.
why.bg: Да обвиняваш други е тревожен сигнал на интервю. Поеми своята част и кажи какво си научил/а.

lines.text: That's refreshingly honest. Now, a slightly awkward one: there's a two-year gap on your CV. Could you talk us through it?

options.text: Of course. I took time out to care for a family member. It was the right decision, and I'm now in a position to commit fully to a new role.
I'd rather not discuss that. It's personal.

why.en: You're entitled to privacy, but shutting the question down sounds defensive. A one-line answer keeps your privacy and their trust.
why.bg: Имаш право на лично пространство, но рязкото отказване звучи защитно. Едно изречение запазва и личното ти пространство, и доверието им.

options.text: Oh, that? I wasn't really doing much, to be honest.

why.en: Vague and casual — it undersells you. Name the reason briefly and link it back to the job.
why.bg: Мъгляво и небрежно — подценяваш се. Посочи накратко причината и я свържи с работата.

objective.en: Answer questions about leaving, salary and your own questions diplomatically.
objective.bg: Да отговориш дипломатично на въпроси за напускане, заплата и твоите собствени въпроси.

explanation.en: Explain a move in terms of what you're going towards, not what you're escaping. On salary, anchor a researched range while keeping room to negotiate. At the end, ask a question that shows you're thinking about doing the job well.
explanation.bg: Обясни смяната с това към какво се стремиш, а не от какво бягаш. За заплатата посочи проучен диапазон, като оставиш място за преговори. Накрая задай въпрос, който показва, че мислиш как да вършиш работата добре.

hints.en: Each wrong option either complains, gives too much away, or shows the wrong priorities.
hints.bg: Всеки грешен вариант или се оплаква, или издава твърде много, или показва грешни приоритети.

scene.en: A second-round interview for a strategy role. Aisha is from HR; Jonathan would be your manager.
scene.bg: Втори кръг на интервю за позиция в стратегически отдел. Айша е от човешки ресурси, а Джонатан ще ти бъде мениджър.

lines.text: So, Stefan, why are you looking to move on after only eighteen months?

options.text: It's a fair question. I've learnt a great deal there, but the role has become fairly narrow, and I'm keen to take on more strategic work — which is exactly what this position offers.
Honestly, my manager is impossible and the whole place is a mess.

why.en: Criticising your current employer makes interviewers wonder what you'll say about them one day.
why.bg: Критиката към сегашния работодател кара интервюиращите да се чудят какво някой ден ще говориш за тях.

options.text: It's a fair question. I want to leave because I've been there since eighteen months.

why.en: Duration takes "for": "for eighteen months". "Since" needs a starting point, like "since 2024".
why.bg: Продължителността се изразява с "for": "for eighteen months". "Since" изисква начален момент, напр. "since 2024".

lines.text: And what sort of salary are you expecting?

options.text: I'd want to understand the full package first, but based on my research, something in the region of sixty to sixty-five thousand would seem reasonable.

why.en: Flippant. It sounds like a joke and gives them nothing to work with.
why.bg: Несериозно. Звучи като шега и не им дава нищо конкретно.

options.text: Anything is fine, really — I'd just be grateful for the job.

why.en: This undersells you and throws away your negotiating position.
why.bg: Така се подценяваш и се отказваш от позицията си за преговори.

lines.text: That's within our range. Finally, is there anything you'd like to ask us?

options.text: Yes, actually — how would you measure success in this role after the first six months?
No, I think you've covered everything.

why.en: A missed opportunity: having no questions can signal low interest.
why.bg: Пропусната възможност: липсата на въпроси може да изглежда като слаб интерес.

options.text: Yes — how much holiday can I take in my first month?

why.en: Premature. Asking about time off first suggests your priorities lie elsewhere.
why.bg: Прибързано. Ако първо питаш за отпуска, изглежда, че приоритетите ти са другаде.

lines.text: Great question. Jonathan, do you want to take that one?

objective.en: Understand a candidate's reflection on a past mistake.
objective.bg: Да разбереш как кандидат анализира минала грешка.

explanation.en: Asked what he'd do differently, Owen says: "Flag the risk much earlier, frankly." To flag a risk = to warn people about it. Flying out, the revised schedule and the check-ins are what he actually did.
explanation.bg: На въпроса какво би направил различно Оуен казва: "Flag the risk much earlier, frankly." To flag a risk = да предупредиш за риск. Пътуването, новият график и седмичните срещи са неща, които той наистина е направил.

hints.bg: Съсредоточи се върху последния отговор на Оуен.

items.audio:
Rachel: Tell me about a time you had to deal with a difficult client.
Owen: A few years back, a major client threatened to pull out of a contract over a missed deadline. Rather than get defensive, I flew out to see them, owned the mistake, and proposed a revised schedule with weekly check-ins. Not only did we keep the account, but they've since doubled their order.
Rachel: And what would you do differently now?
Owen: Flag the risk much earlier, frankly.
items.question: What does Owen think he should have done?
options: Warned about the risk much earlier
Flown out to meet the client sooner
Offered weekly check-ins from the beginning
Refused to accept a revised schedule

explanation.en: "I wouldn't go as far as to call myself fluent" plus "I can hold my own in meetings" means confident speaking without claiming perfection; "written Spanish is more of a work in progress" means her writing is weaker.
explanation.bg: "I wouldn't go as far as to call myself fluent" (не бих казала, че говоря свободно) плюс "I can hold my own in meetings" (справям се на срещи) значи увереност в говоренето без претенции за съвършенство; "written Spanish is more of a work in progress" значи, че писането ѝ е по-слабо.

hints.en: Listen for how she contrasts speaking and writing.
hints.bg: Слушай как противопоставя говоренето и писането.

items.audio:
Gareth: How would you rate your Spanish?
Nadia: I wouldn't go as far as to call myself fluent, but I can hold my own in meetings, and I've handled supplier negotiations in Spanish — albeit with the odd slip. Written Spanish is more of a work in progress, if I'm honest.
Gareth: That's useful to know. Most of the role is spoken, anyway.
items.question: How does Nadia describe her Spanish?
options: Confident in speaking, weaker in writing
Fluent in both speaking and writing
Good in writing, but she avoids meetings

objective.en: Repeat a modest but confident claim.
objective.bg: Да повториш скромно, но уверено твърдение.

explanation.en: "I wouldn't say I'm an expert, but…" lowers the claim slightly so that what follows sounds credible.
explanation.bg: "I wouldn't say I'm an expert, but…" леко смекчава твърдението, за да звучи следващото убедително.

hints.en: "Picked up" here means "learnt without formal study".
hints.bg: "Picked up" тук значи "научил/а съм в движение, без официално обучение".

items.prompt: I wouldn't say I'm an expert, but I've picked up a fair amount along the way.
items.model: I wouldn't say I'm an expert, but I've picked up a fair amount along the way.
items.target: I wouldn't say I'm an expert, but I've picked up a fair amount along the way.

objective.bg: Да прочетеш на глас отговор с поглед назад.

explanation.en: "With hindsight, I'd have…" (third conditional meaning) shows reflection without dramatic self-criticism.
explanation.bg: "With hindsight, I'd have…" (значение на трето условно) показва самоанализ без драматична самокритика.

items.prompt: With hindsight, I'd have delegated more; at the time, I felt I had to oversee every detail myself.
items.model: With hindsight, I'd have delegated more; at the time, I felt I had to oversee every detail myself.
items.target: With hindsight, I'd have delegated more; at the time, I felt I had to oversee every detail myself.

objective.en: Name a strength and back it up with an example.
objective.bg: Да назовеш силна страна и да я подкрепиш с пример.

explanation.en: Name one strength, then prove it with a short real example: the situation, what you did and the result. An example is far more convincing than a list of adjectives.
explanation.bg: Назови една силна страна и я докажи с кратък истински пример: ситуацията, какво направи и резултата. Един пример убеждава много повече от списък с прилагателни.

hints.en: Try: "I'd say my greatest strength is… For example, when…"
hints.bg: Опитай: "I'd say my greatest strength is… For example, when…"

items.prompt: What would you say is your greatest strength? Give an example.
items.model: I'd say my greatest strength is staying calm under pressure. For example, when our main supplier went bust last year, I found two alternatives within a week.

explanation.en: "Despite" is never followed by "of". Say "despite the deadline" or "in spite of the deadline" — the "of" belongs only to "in spite of".
explanation.bg: След "despite" никога не идва "of". Казва се "despite the deadline" или "in spite of the deadline" — "of" има само в "in spite of".

items.sentence: Despite of the tight deadline, we delivered the project on budget.
accept: Despite the tight deadline, we delivered the project on budget.
In spite of the tight deadline, we delivered the project on budget.
